newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta stock exchange recovers losses.
newsitem.headline: Malta stock exchange recovers losses.

text.p: Heavy trading in government bonds and an increase in the average price of bank shares characterised Wednesday's trading session of the Malta stock exchange, with the share index shooting up by 20 points, recovering losses made in the past three weeks
Turnover in the once-weekly session reached over Lm5.3 million ($13.78 million), from last weeks Lm452,000.
Government bonds accounted for Lm5.2 million of the trading, a bourse official said.
There were 135 deals, of which 47 were in equities and 88 in fixed income securities. The value of the index rose to 986.71.
Business in equities amounted to just over Lm72,400, with 54,100 shares being transacted.
The biggest gains were in Bank of Valletta, where 23,200 shares were sold for an average 123 cents per share, up five cents from last week.
There were 17 deals in Mid-Med Bank, with 18,700 shares selling for an average 154 cents, up four cents.
There were five deals in Lombard Bank Malta, with 10,000 shares changing hands for an average 140 cents per share, up one cent.
The only loss was in Farsons, where 2,200 shares changed hands for an average 49 cents per share, down one cent.

Trading in government bonds involved 15 issues, with business in the 6.23 per cent MGS 1999 (IV); the six per cent MGS 1998 (VI) and the 7.25 per cent 2006 (III) acounting for over 67 per cent of turnover in bonds.
There was one deal in the 6.5 per cent Gasan bonds 1998/99 amounting to Lm492.50 and two deals in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 per cent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to Lm1,300. Prices were unchanged.
